title: Abhimanyu's last stand
hookLine: a young warrior with no bow, no horses and no sword picks up a chariot wheel
carry: dharma has rules, even in war
tomorrow: can Arjuna reach Jayadratha before the sun sets?

lines: NO BOW, NO HORSES, NO SWORD.
cards: He has no bow anymore. His horses are down, his charioteer is gone, his sword is broken. And Abhimanyu bends down and picks up a chariot wheel, lifts it like a weapon, and keeps fighting.
That picture is where the day ends up. It starts with him tearing through the Kaurava ranks inside the formation, so fiercely that, in Ganguli's telling, even Drona speaks admiringly of his skill.
Today, the end of Abhimanyu, and the promise his father makes that night.

teach.b: Drona admires the boy, and still commands: take his bow first. Karna cuts it from behind. Others bring down his horses and his charioteer.
Then the great warriors of the Kaurava side close around one young man together. Abhimanyu fights on with sword and shield until they break, then with the chariot wheel, then with a mace.

At last the son of Duhshasana strikes him down. Here's why Hindus remember this as one of the war's darkest hours. Before the first arrow flew, both sides agreed on rules for a righteous war, a dharma yuddha.
Fight your equal, one to one. Never strike someone whose weapon is broken, who has no armor, who is already fighting another.
Abhimanyu died against nearly every one of them.

teach.h: THE RULES OF A RIGHTEOUS WAR
teach.b: The teaching: dharma doesn't switch off in a war. Even in the worst place, there's a right way and a wrong way, and the epic keeps the account.
Days later, when Karna's own chariot wheel sinks in the mud and he pleads for a fair fight, Krishna asks him where that dharma was when many surrounded the boy.
That evening, Arjuna rides back and senses something is wrong before anyone speaks. When he learns his son is dead, and that Jayadratha held the gap, his grief becomes a vow.
Before tomorrow's sun sets, he'll kill Jayadratha, and if he fails, he'll enter the fire himself.

how: Abhimanyu's last stand is told in the Drona Parva and remembered in retellings, songs and stage plays, where he is honored for his courage and his death is told as a breach of the rules of righteous war.

o: the father who vows revenge before the next sunset
the Kaurava who cuts Abhimanyu's bow from behind his back
the teacher commanding the army that closes in on Abhimanyu

games.q: Abhimanyu's last fight — tap the pairs.

s: Abhimanyu was defeated in a fair one-on-one fight
many great warriors closed around him together.
the Kurukshetra war had no rules at all
before it began, both sides agreed on rules of a righteous war, a dharma yuddha; Abhimanyu was killed against them.
Arjuna vowed to kill Jayadratha before the next sunset
and to enter the fire himself if he failed.

games.q: you're Karna. Drona says take the boy's bow first, and the only way is from behind. the agreed rules of dharma yuddha forbid it. what does dharma ask?
o: refuse: a fair fight or none.
cut it from behind; winning matters more.
cut it, then leave the rest to others.
games.why: Karna cut it from behind. days later, when his own chariot wheel sank, Krishna reminded him of the boy surrounded by many.

practice: If you'd like, rest one hand over your heart and bring to mind someone young you care about: a child, a niece, a student, a younger friend. Many Hindus close a prayer with three words: om shanti, shanti, shanti.
Peace, peace, peace. Breathe in and picture them clearly. Breathe out and say it, once for them, once for the world around them, once for your own heart.
If someone you loved died too young, let them be here too, gently. If you don't pray, let the words simply be a wish.

wordCard.voice: Drona. Today his army closes in on Abhimanyu, against the rules of a righteous war, and Arjuna answers with a vow before sunset.

orig.note: righteous war: a war fought by agreed rules of dharma.

carryVoice: Your line: dharma has rules, even in war. The week ends on a father's vow, with a sunset still to come. Until tomorrow.
